Your task is to generate a complete research paper using the materials below.
You must produce:
1. A BibTeX bibliography file (references.bib)
2. The full LaTeX paper (template.tex)

Instructions
• Use the research idea and experimental logs to construct a coherent, rigorous ML paper.
• For related work and baselines:
  – Search for and include influential papers published up until 2024-11.
  – Incorporate relevant literature and add the corresponding BibTeX entries to references.bib.
  – Do NOT hallucinate papers or reference keys; all citation entries must be real.
• In the LaTeX paper, cite papers using \cite{} with keys that match exactly with your entries in references.bib.
• Do not fabricate experimental results or make claims unsupported by the logs.

Materials
Here are all the raw research materials to assist with the writing process:

[RESEARCH IDEA]
## Problem Statement
Visual localization—determining the precise 6-DoF camera pose of a query image relative to a known database—currently suffers from a significant trade-off between accuracy, efficiency, and generalizability. Traditional structure-based methods (Structure-from-Motion) offer high accuracy but are computationally expensive and slow at inference time, limiting their use in real-time robotics or AR. Conversely, Absolute Pose Regression (APR) approaches are fast but inherently scene-specific; they fail to generalize to new environments without retraining. While Relative Pose Regression (RPR) attempts to bridge this gap, current methods still lag behind APR in accuracy and often struggle to balance generalization with precise localization. There is a lack of a unified framework that is simultaneously fast, accurate, and capable of zero-shot transfer to novel scenes.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose that the limitations of current pose regression methods stem from unnecessary complexity in handling metric scales and asymmetric processing of image pairs. We hypothesize that a **fully symmetric, scale-invariant relative pose regression network**, when scaled up with massive diverse training data, can learn robust geometric relationships superior to scene-specific models.

Our core intuition is two-fold:
1.  **Parsimony in Learning:** By training the network to predict only the *direction* of translation (treating it as an angular problem similar to rotation) rather than the metric scale, we simplify the learning landscape and avoid biases introduced by varying scene scales.
2.  **Symmetry:** A Siamese-style architecture that processes image pairs symmetrically (sharing weights and ignoring order) captures the relative geometry more naturally than asymmetric designs.

## Proposed Methodology (High-Level Technical Approach)
We aim to develop a streamlined framework consisting of two distinct stages: a deep relative pose regressor and a minimalist deterministic solver.

**1. Symmetric Relative Pose Regression Network**
We will design a deep neural network based on a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone. The workflow is as follows:
*   **Input Processing:** The system takes a query image and a set of retrieved database images. These are processed as independent pairs.
*   **Token Interaction:** We will utilize a standard encoder-decoder structure where image patches are converted to tokens. Crucially, we will employ **cross-attention mechanisms** in the decoder layers. This allows the network to reason about the spatial correspondence and flow between the query and the database image tokens effectively.
*   **Symmetric Architecture:** The network branches will be fully symmetric with shared weights. It will predict the relative pose from Image A to Image B and simultaneously from B to A. This enforces consistency and reduces parameter count.
*   **Scale-Free Regression Heads:** The output heads will regress the relative rotation and the *direction* of the translation vector. We will not ask the network to predict metric depth. The loss function will be designed to minimize angular errors for both rotation and translation directions, normalizing the translation vectors to focus purely on orientation.

**2. Minimalist Motion Averaging Module**
Once the network provides relative pose estimates (rotation and translation direction) for the query against multiple database images, we will resolve the absolute pose and metric scale analytically:
*   **Rotation Averaging:** We will aggregate the predicted relative rotations to solve for the absolute rotation. To ensure robustness against outliers from the retrieval step, we will employ a median-based averaging strategy rather than a simple mean.
*   **Camera Center Triangulation:** Since the network outputs translation *directions*, the query camera center lies along specific rays originating from the database camera centers. We will determine the absolute query position by finding the optimal intersection point of these rays using a linear least-squares method (via Singular Value Decomposition). This mathematically resolves the metric scale without requiring the network to learn it explicitly.

## Expected Contribution
The proposed research aims to deliver the following contributions:
*   **Theoretical Value:** Validating that metric scale estimation is better handled by geometric triangulation than by deep learning, thereby simplifying the task for neural networks.
*   **Generalization:** A single, foundation-model-style framework capable of localizing in diverse environments (indoor, outdoor, object-centric) without any scene-specific fine-tuning.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** Achieving high-accuracy localization suitable for real-time applications (milliseconds inference time), surpassing the speed of structure-based methods while matching their utility in unseen environments.

[EXPERIMENTAL LOGS]
## 1. Experimental Setup

We established a comprehensive training and evaluation pipeline for a relative camera pose regression framework named Reloc3r. The system included a relative pose regression network based on a Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture and a motion averaging module for absolute pose estimation.

### Training Data Configuration
We constructed a large-scale training dataset comprising approximately eight million image pairs with ground-truth relative poses.
*   **Source Datasets:** CO3Dv2 (Object-centric), ScanNet++ (Indoor), ARKitScenes (Indoor), BlendedMVS (Outdoor), MegaDepth (Outdoor), DL3DV (Indoor & Outdoor), and RealEstate10K (Indoor & Outdoor).
*   **Preprocessing:** Ground-truth relative poses were converted to a unified relative coordinate transformation format aligned with OpenCV definitions. Images were center-cropped based on principal points and resized to a width of 512 pixels.

### Model Architecture & Implementation
*   **Backbone:** Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture inspired by DUSt3R, featuring a fully symmetric design with shared weights between branches.
*   **Encoder:** 24 blocks.
*   **Decoder:** 12 blocks (initialized with DUSt3R decoder2 weights).
*   **Regression Head:** 2 convolutional layers.
*   **Optimizations:** Utilized memory-efficient attention (FlashAttention) achieving ~14% speed increase and 25% memory saving.
*   **Hardware:** Trained on 8 AMD MI250x-40G GPUs. Evaluation conducted on a single 24GB NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPU.
*   **Hyperparameters:**
    *   Batch size: 8.
    *   Learning Rate: Started at 1e-5, decayed to 1e-7.
    *   Precision: Mixed precision fp16/fp32.
*   **Loss Function:** Minimized difference between predicted relative angles and ground truth for both rotation and translation directions.

### Evaluation Setup
*   **Retrieval Method:** NetVLAD was used to retrieve the top-10 similar database images for each query image. No distance-based clustering or filtering was applied.
*   **Task 1: Relative Pose Estimation Metrics:**
    *   **Pair-wise:** Area Under Curve (AUC) at thresholds of 5, 10, and 20 degrees (AUC@5, AUC@10, AUC@20).
    *   **Multi-view:** Relative Rotation Accuracy within 15 degrees (RRA@15), Relative Translation Accuracy within 15 degrees (RTA@15), and Mean Average Accuracy at 30 degrees (mAA@30).
*   **Task 2: Visual Localization Metrics:** Median translation error (meters) and median rotation error (degrees).
*   **Baselines Compared:**
    *   *Non-Pose Regression (Non-PR):* PixSfM, RelPose, PoseDiffusion, RelPose++, RayDiffusion, VGGSfM, DUSt3R (w/ PnP), MASt3R, Efficient LoFTR, ROMA, NoPoSplat.
    *   *Pose Regression (PR/APR/RPR):* PoseReg, RayReg, Map-free (Match & Regress), ExReNet (SN & SUNCG), LENS, PMNet, DFNet+NeFeS, Marepo, EssNet, Relative PN, RelocNet, Relpose-GNN, AnchorNet, CamNet, ImageNet+NCM.

*   **Observation 1 (Accuracy vs. Efficiency):** In the ScanNet1500 comparison (AUC@5 vs. FPS), Reloc3r-512 achieved the highest AUC@5 (~35) while maintaining real-time efficiency (24 FPS). The 224-resolution variant matched the accuracy of the ROMA method but operated 20 times faster.
*   **Observation 2 (Feature Correlation):** Visualizations of cross-attention responses revealed that Reloc3r's decoder layers implicitly learned to identify and match patch correspondences between image pairs, despite the model being trained solely with pose supervision (relative angles) and no explicit feature matching loss.
*   **Observation 3 (Correspondence Quality):** Qualitative comparison against Efficient LoFTR showed that Reloc3r produced superior correlated regions, particularly in challenging scenarios where explicit matchers struggled.
*   **Observation 4 (Visual Trajectory Alignment):** On 7 Scenes (Chess) and Cambridge Landmarks (KingsCollege), the absolute pose estimates from Reloc3r aligned more closely with ground-truth trajectories than competing Relative Pose Regression (RPR) methods like ExReNet and Map-free.
*   **Observation 5 (Failure Mode):** A specific degeneracy issue was identified where the metric scale becomes unsolvable by the motion averaging module if the query image and all retrieved database images are perfectly collinear.

Role: Senior AI Researcher and Academic Writer.
Objective: Complete a machine learning research paper by filling in missing sections of a provided LaTeX template and generating a corresponding bibliography file. You must produce a scientifically sound, well-structured paper suitable for submission to a top-tier ML conference.

Inputs
You will receive the following materials:
• idea.md: Detailed description of the proposed method and technical ideas.
• experimental_log.md: Raw experimental results and observations used to construct tables, figures, and analysis.
• conference_guidelines.md: Formatting and stylistic requirements for the target conference.
• figures_list: A list of figures that may be referenced in the paper.

Conference Guidelines
# CVPR 2025 Paper Writing Guidelines

Below are the instructions to help you with the latex paper writing process for CVPR 2025.

## Language
All manuscripts must be in English.

## Submission Policies & Anonymity
CVPR reviewing is double-blind. Authors must not know the names of the reviewers, and reviewers must not know the names of the authors.

* **No Identifying Information:** Do not provide information that may identify the authors in the acknowledgments (e.g., co-workers and grant IDs) or in the supplementary material.
* **Links:** Do not provide links to websites that identify the authors.
* **GitHub:** Links to GitHub must be anonymous.
* **Self-Citation:** If you need to cite any of your own papers that are being submitted concurrently, include anonymized versions in the supplementary material and cite them as anonymous. Do not use the words "my" or "our" when citing previous work; treat your own prior work as if it were written by someone else (e.g., "Smith et al. showed..." rather than "We showed...").

## Paper length

references.text:
## Problem Statement
Visual localization—determining the 6-DoF camera pose of a query image relative to a known database—currently faces a dichotomy between accuracy and efficiency. Traditional structure-based methods (matching pixels to 3D models) offer high accuracy but suffer from slow inference times and poor scalability due to the need for geometric optimization (SfM) and 3D scene reconstruction. Conversely, Absolute Pose Regression (APR) methods allow for fast inference but are inherently scene-specific, requiring dense viewpoint coverage during training and lacking generalization to new environments.

Existing Relative Pose Regression (RPR) approaches attempt to bridge this gap by estimating poses between image pairs. However, current RPR methods lag significantly behind APR in accuracy and often struggle to generalize effectively without doubling localization errors on novel scenes. There is a critical need for a framework that combines the speed of regression methods with the generalization capabilities of foundation models, without the computational overhead of novel view synthesis or complex robust estimation pipelines.

## Core Hypothesis
We propose **Reloc3r**, a visual localization framework built on the hypothesis that a parsimonious, fully symmetric deep neural network trained on massive scale (approx. 8 million image pairs) can outperform complex, scene-specific models.

Our core technical hypotheses are:
1.  **Symmetry in Regression:** Unlike asymmetric architectures used for coordinate alignment, a fully symmetric Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with shared weights is optimal for relative pose estimation, as it eliminates ordering bias and reduces computational complexity.
2.  **Scale-Agnostic Supervision:** By training the network to regress the *direction* of translation rather than metric scale, we can utilize diverse datasets with varying scales. The metric scale can be recovered deterministically post-inference.
3.  **Minimalist Aggregation:** High-quality pairwise regression estimates allow us to replace complex RANSAC-based robust estimators with a simple, differentiable motion averaging module (Median Rotation and SVD-based triangulation) to resolve absolute pose.

## Proposed Methodology (Detailed Technical Approach)

We will develop a two-stage framework: a **Relative Pose Regression Network** followed by a **Motion Averaging Module**.

### 1. Relative Pose Regression Network
We will adopt a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone. The network will accept a pair of images, $I_1$ and $I_2$, and output the relative pose transformations $P_{I_1, I_2}$ and $P_{I_2, I_1}$.

**Architecture Specification:**
*   **Tokenization:** Images will be divided into patches and processed as sequences of $T$ tokens with dimension $d$. We will apply RoPE (Rotary Positional Embeddings) to encode spatial information.
*   **ViT Encoder:** We will employ a Siamese encoder structure with $m=24$ blocks. Both branches share identical weights. The encoder processes tokens via self-attention and feed-forward layers to produce encoded features $F_1$ and $F_2$:
    $$ F_i^{(T \times d)} = \mathrm{Encoder}(\mathrm{Patchify}(I_i^{(H \times W \times 3)})), \quad \text{for } i \in \{1, 2\} $$
*   **ViT Decoder:** We will utilize a decoder with $n=12$ blocks. Crucially, each decoder block will incorporate a **cross-attention layer** to facilitate information exchange between the tokens of the two images. This allows the model to reason about spatial relationships:
    $$ \begin{array}{r} G_1^{(T \times d)} = \mathrm{Decoder}(F_1^{(T \times d)}, F_2^{(T \times d)}) \\ G_2^{(T \times d)} = \mathrm{Decoder}(F_2^{(T \times d)}, F_1^{(T \times d)}) \end{array} $$
*   **Regression Head:** The output tokens $G$ will be processed by a head consisting of $h=2$ feed-forward layers followed by average pooling.
*   **Output Formatting:** The head will predict rotation (initially as a 9D representation, converted to a $3 \times 3$ matrix via SVD orthogonalization) and a 3D translation vector.

**Loss Formulation:**
We will treat both rotation and translation errors as angular deviations. We define the total loss $\mathcal{L}$ as:
$$ \mathcal{L} = \ell_R + \ell_t $$

The rotation loss $\ell_R$ minimizes the geodesic distance on SO(3):
$$ \ell_R = \arccos \left( \frac{\operatorname{tr}(\hat{R}^{-1} R) - 1}{2} \right) $$
where $\operatorname{tr}(\cdot)$ is the matrix trace, $\hat{R}$ is the predicted rotation, and $R$ is the ground truth.

The translation loss $\ell_t$ minimizes the angular error between the predicted translation direction $\hat{t}$ and the ground truth $t$:
$$ \ell_t = \arccos \left( \frac{\hat{t} \cdot t}{\| \hat{t} \| \| t \|} \right) $$
This formulation explicitly ignores the metric magnitude of the translation vector during the learning phase, focusing solely on directionality.

### 2. Motion Averaging Module
To recover the absolute pose of a query image $I_q$ relative to the database $D$, we will retrieve top-$K$ pairs and aggregate the pairwise predictions. We will not use RANSAC or iterative optimization; instead, we will use deterministic linear algebra.

**Rotation Averaging:**
Given a relative rotation prediction $\hat{R}_{q, d_i}$ between the query and the $i$-th database image (with known pose $R_{d_i}$), the candidate absolute rotation is $\hat{R}_q = R_{d_i} \hat{R}_{q, d_i}$. We will aggregate estimates from all $K$ pairs by computing the **median rotation** (via quaternion representation) to ensure robustness against outliers.

**Camera Center Triangulation:**
To solve for the absolute translation (and scale), we will perform triangulation. We formulate this as a least-squares problem minimizing the sum of squared distances from the unknown camera center to the translation directions predicted by the network.
*   We define the predicted relative translation direction as a ray.
*   We will solve for the intersection of these rays using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD).

### 3. Implementation Plan
*   **Data Scale:** We will curate a training dataset of approximately 8 million image pairs from diverse sources (e.g., ScanNet, MegaDepth, CO3D) to cover object-centric, indoor, and outdoor scenes.
*   **Efficiency:** We will implement memory-efficient attention mechanisms to handle the token load of the Transformer backbone, aiming for a test-time efficiency of >20 FPS.

## Expected Contribution
1.  **Unified Generalization:** By training on a massive, diverse dataset with a scale-agnostic loss, we expect the model to generalize zero-shot to novel scenes without the need for scene-specific retraining (unlike APRs) or depth maps (unlike scene coordinate regression).
2.  **Architectural Parsimony:** We demonstrate that a symmetric, "foundation model" approach to pose regression can replace complex geometric pipelines.
3.  **Real-Time Performance:** The elimination of expensive iterative robust estimators (like RANSAC or PnP loops) in favor of a single-pass ViT and SVD-based averaging will enable real-time localization suitable for robotics and AR.

notes.extra_model_calls: WebFetch runs a secondary extraction model call inside Claude Code; counted in modelUsage

network.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
network.web_access: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.

tools.permissions: upstream's own agent settings; provider web search denied by managed settings (Claude Code permissions.deny WebSearch, Codex web_search="disabled")

preinstalled.zh: 编排镜像：上游代码（固定提交、未改）、uv 锁定依赖、docker CLI（经 shim 给兄弟容器加代理和 CA）；agent 镜像：上游自己的 agent-cli Dockerfile
preinstalled.en: orchestrator image: upstream code at the pin (unmodified), uv-locked dependencies, the docker CLI (a shim adds proxy and CA to sibling containers); agent image: upstream's own agent-cli Dockerfile

notes.benchmark_paths: A benchmark item's paths are mounted into the agent containers unless upstream mounts the same path itself (/workspace and below, /home/agent-home, /task-source, /run, /tmp): those are left out and listed in logs/sibling-mounts.txt. The agents work in upstream's own /workspace (the run directory), so a deliverable the official prompt names under such a path is not written where the run collects it.
notes.venue: paper.paper_format=iclr for every task. The system has only iclr and alife specs and does not choose a venue itself; ICML and NeurIPS templates and a system-chosen venue are unsupported.
notes.task_input: Only the `# Goal` and `# Rubrics` sections of task.md are read: all five candidate files are put under `# Goal` with their headings turned into bold lines; `# Rubrics` carries a neutral line. The paradigm is optimisation of a scalar score: the task-drafting phase (documented as experimental) turns the brief into an evaluator and a seed program.
notes.phases: execution.phases=task_drafting,investigation,final_evaluation,paper; the system's own default also runs ablations and posthoc; final_evaluation stays because a drafted task requires it before the paper. review/revision (second model) are never selected.
notes.agent_pool: agent.pool and agent.models.* are left empty: one model for every phase.
notes.second_provider: No OPENAI/GEMINI key is supplied (concept figures stay in deterministic export mode).
notes.time: No global wall-clock or token cap exists upstream; the runner enforces time_limit_hours. Native caps used: idea cycles=3, per-phase timeouts from [systems.agentic-scientist].
notes.network: Sibling agent containers run on the shield's internal network; the agents keep their CLI WebFetch/Bash network, which go through the shield. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield.
notes.search: Provider server-side web search is switched off in every sibling by the agent CLIs' own system settings, bind-mounted read-only by the docker shim: Claude Code /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (permissions.deny WebSearch), Codex /etc/codex/config.toml (web_search="disabled") and /etc/codex/requirements.toml (allowed_web_search_modes=["disabled"]). Upstream's own Semantic Scholar client goes through the shield.
notes.key_exposure: The provider key is in the environment of the agent containers (upstream env-file mechanism) and therefore visible to commands the agent runs. Claude Code's CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 was tried and aborts: it needs bubblewrap, which the unmodified upstream agent image lacks.
notes.gpu: gpus=1 is wired (container.gpu_count, harness GPU evaluation) but was not exercised.
notes.docker_socket: The orchestrator container has the host docker socket (root-equivalent on the host).

agent.name: none
agent.how: no coding agent: a 23-stage prompt-chain pipeline over the Anthropic Messages API

network.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).

tools.permissions: no tool calls (requests carry model, messages, max_tokens); generated experiments run as plain subprocesses in the container

preinstalled.zh: python:3.11 bookworm；上游代码按 PYTHONPATH 使用；pdflatex + bibtex；CPU 版 PyTorch 和 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn、pandas、matplotlib 等（constraints.txt 固定）
preinstalled.en: python:3.11 bookworm; upstream code via PYTHONPATH; pdflatex + bibtex; CPU PyTorch with numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib and more (pinned by constraints.txt)

notes.model: claude-opus-5-5 through the Anthropic Messages API (llm.provider=anthropic), no fallback models, reviewer model = same model. Requests carry model, messages and max_tokens only (no tools, no thinking parameter); ARC's per-stage temperature is not sent because the model rejects it, so the API default applies.
notes.agent: ARC is not a tool-using coding agent: its 23-stage pipeline, its own code agent and its reviewers are prompt chains over plain chat completions. conditions.agent=claude means only that the provider is Anthropic; Claude Code is not involved. Generated experiments run as a plain subprocess in the container.
notes.effort: ARC has no effort setting; usage-log.patch sends output_config.effort='high' with every request. Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and ARC's per-stage max_tokens (for example 4096) is shared with the thinking tokens, so long outputs can still be cut short.
notes.venue: Not chosen by the system: export.target_conference=iclr_2026 comes from [systems.autoresearchclaw].
notes.tokens: ARC records no usage. A logging-only patch (usage-log.patch) appends each Messages API `usage` block to anthropic-usage.jsonl; cost is not computed. The same patch carries the RWE_OMIT_TEMPERATURE and RWE_EFFORT switches.
notes.time: No global wall-clock or budget cap in ARC; only the runner's limit applies. Per experiment run 3600 s, refinement iterations 10, repair cycles 3.
notes.input: Chinese pack text goes verbatim (candidate files concatenated, with <!-- file --> markers) into prompts.extra_prompts of 18 stages. ARC takes one topic string and checks generated code against it, so research.topic is the candidate TASK.md verbatim with whitespace collapsed. Literature queries come from the stage-3 model plan; ARC's ASCII keyword splitter and its whitespace-based query expansion yield a few useless queries from the Chinese text. Starter papers are guidance text only: ARC cannot ingest seed papers.
notes.search: Web search, crawling, GitHub, HF Hub, Gemini and OpenCode are off. Literature search in stage 4 uses ['openalex', 'semantic_scholar'] through ARC's own clients behind the shield proxy; stages 8, 17, 22 and 23 (novelty, citation verification) always also query arXiv, CrossRef and DataCite; the shield date-bounds those API calls like the others (a late DOI answers 403).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: every request to api.anthropic.com is built in researchclaw/llm/anthropic_adapter.py:136-148 and carries only model, messages, max_tokens, optional temperature, output_config.effort and system, never a tools or web_search field; the OpenAI-compatible client (OpenRouter :online / plugins) is not used (llm.provider=anthropic), web_search.enabled=false, Gemini is only used by the disabled figure_agent.nano_banana. Provider hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so such a path would be invisible to the audit.
notes.secrets: Generated experiment code inherits the container environment, including the API keys (ARC offers no switch to scrub it).
notes.profile: project.profile=ml_generic is fixed for all tasks; research.domains is left empty because the literature screen rejects papers outside the stated domain (a theory task failed with domains=[machine-learning]).

agent.name: none
agent.how: no external coding agent: EvoScientist's in-process sub-agents (LangChain deepagents)

tools.permissions: think_tool, deepagents built-ins, EvoSkills skills and an execute shell; skill_manager not registered; no search tool

preinstalled.zh: 上游锁定依赖（uv sync --frozen）加兼容补丁 compat.patch；TeX Live（含 fonts-extra、latexmk）；给 agent 用的研究 Python 环境 /opt/research
preinstalled.en: upstream's locked dependencies (uv sync --frozen) plus compat.patch; TeX Live (with fonts-extra and latexmk); a research Python environment for the agent in /opt/research

notes.agent: No external coding agent: EvoScientist runs its own in-process planner/research/code/debug/writing sub-agents (LangChain deepagents) on the one configured model. conditions.agent only selects the provider; Claude Code and Codex are not used.
notes.model: Main agent, sub-agents and EvoScientist's auxiliary calls (tool selector, memory workers, summariser, graders) all use the configured model; auxiliary_model and model_fallbacks are empty.
notes.effort: Upstream hard-wires effort=max and max_tokens=128000 for Anthropic models. compat.patch makes the effort come from EVOSCIENTIST_REASONING_EFFORT (= conditions.effort); max_tokens stays 128000 (a cap, not a cost driver). Adaptive thinking (display=summarized) is upstream and not switchable.
notes.paper: The core writes a Markdown report (final_report.md); the EvoSkills paper-writing skill gives a generic LaTeX `article` skeleton with no ICML/ICLR/NeurIPS style and no compile step. The image has TeX Live (latexmk, fonts-extra) but no venue style files; the task asks for an official template, so a venue-formatted PDF depends on the agent obtaining the style through the shield. No extra pipeline stage was added; absent items are listed in result.missing.
notes.tools: skill_manager (git clone of any repository as a skill) is not registered (compat.patch); the Tavily key is not set so tavily_search does not exist; LANGGRAPH_CLI_NO_ANALYTICS=1; EvoSkills is baked in at its pinned commit. The execute shell and the EvoSkills paper-navigator scripts reach the world only through the shield; S2_DATE_CUTOFF is not set (the shield bounds dates).
notes.server_side_search: Not reachable: EvoScientist binds no provider-side search tool to any model (its only tools are think_tool, tavily_search when TAVILY_API_KEY is set, MCP tools from mcp.yaml, deepagents built-ins and skills; EvoScientist/EvoScientist.py:671-672 and 754-755 at the pin; the one bind_tools call is the tool selector's own output schema, middleware/tool_selector.py:166). TAVILY_API_KEY is not passed and the image has no mcp.yaml, so no search tool exists. Anthropic/OpenAI hosts are only tunnelled by the shield, so a provider-side search would be invisible to the audit.
notes.credentials: The provider key is in the process environment and EvoScientist's execute shell inherits the environment (upstream has no switch); the key is therefore visible to the agent's shell. It is a run-scoped copy and is not logged by this adapter.
notes.memory: A fresh data dir per run (baked skills, empty memory). Memory workers, skill synthesis and the scheduler stay at upstream defaults, so their LLM calls count in the usage log.
notes.limits: async sub-agents off (README advice for scripted runs); recursion_limit=1000000; model retry wait in auto-mode 1800 s (time without progress counts as wall time); execute timeout 300 s per command. No token or cost budget exists.
